title: Painting keeps up with the pointer on a 12 megapixel picture, measured
goal: Painting never lags behind your hand, even on a big photo: the stroke under the pointer draws within a frame and letting go lands the stroke without a hitch, measured on a 12 megapixel picture with a few hundred strokes on its paint layer.
notes:
Umbrella: a-brush-tool-paints-with-realistic-charcoal-chal (the user's ask, 2026-10-24). Design: docs/design/brushes.md, read it first; its decisions are settled unless this task's runner finds one cannot work, in which case they say so in the log and in the doc.

Design doc decision 5. Needs the medium slices for the per-medium numbers; the foundation slice may already do the prefix cache.
acceptance: Input-to-pixel latency and frame time while painting are measured on a 12 MP picture with each medium, and are under one frame (16 ms) for the live stroke
Landing a stroke on a paint layer that already holds a few hundred strokes takes under 50 ms (the layer keeps its last raster and paints only the new stroke)
Undo of a stroke on that layer is as quick as landing one
The numbers are written in the audit and held by a perf test
Zoomed in to 200% on a 12 MP canvas, a stroke looks the same after the button comes up as while it was held (the walk's held-to-landed check passes at that zoom)

log.note: deps set by the umbrella's planning run: pressing-b-picks-a-brush-that-paints-freehand-st, charcoal-chalk-and-crayon-catch-on-a-paper-grain, marker-strokes-are-flat-and-darken-where-they-cr, watercolour-strokes-are-transparent-pool-darker, oil-paint-strokes-carry-and-smear-colour-and-sho

Measured 2026-10-25 by the watercolour walk (watercolour-wash-and-bloom-walk, 4000x3000 canvas): painting moves 0.4-0.9 ms median, 1.8 ms worst, but each stroke landing holds the main thread 344-432 ms (wait notes 'longest 431.9ms') while the whole Paint layer is replayed; pencil-draws-and-shades-walk shows the same 315-414 ms. Watercolour adds one thing to keep in mind for the cached raster: a watercolour stroke blooms into earlier strokes still wet at its start (BrushStroke.wetness(when:), WetWashes in Watercolour.swift), so painting only stroke n onto a cached raster needs the wet fields of the strokes still wet, which WetWashes.under(_:earlier:toPixels:limit:) already rebuilds for the live overlay.

From the oil paint slice (2026-10-25): DocumentRenderer bakes a paint layer at crispScale(contentScale, box: layer box), capped at 16 MP, and a Paint layer is the whole canvas, so on a 4000x3000 canvas a landed stroke is ~1.15 px/pt while the live overlay draws at screen resolution. Reproduced: Scripts/playtest/oil-paint-smears-and-ridges-walk.json with 8 zoomIn steps (displayZoom 172) fails step 24 'the picture jumped on the release: 1.3% of the canvas differs'; at 7 steps (138%) 0.73%; at 6 (110%) 0.42%. Every medium softens on release when zoomed in; oil's bristles show it most. Likely fix: bake only the strokes' bounds (or tiles) so the cap is spent where the paint is.
